purpose: Demonstrate that the interval-algebra implementation returns the exact admissible integer-start set and samples uniformly from it before full Phase-A execution.
deterministic_fixtures: single chain block, no exclusions, one hg38 PU.1 interval, one NIH peak
candidate band crossing chain-block boundary: only exact-roundtrip starts survive
ambiguous/multiple forward mapping: all affected starts excluded
promoter-specific distal exclusion splits one admissible interval into two
empty drawn side while opposite side is non-empty: draw fails and does not retry
CONTROL_A and CONTROL_B independent sub-seeds can coincide and coincidence is retained
anchor_frequency counts distinct overlapping promoter_keys rather than edges or exact starts

oracle.fixture_method: For small synthetic coordinate ranges, enumerate every integer start by brute force and apply the authoritative gates one start at a time.
oracle.required_equivalence: Interval-algebra admissible set must equal the brute-force set exactly: same cardinality and identical sorted starts.

real_edge_checks.rule: Before full execution, select a deterministic outcome-blind sample of real structural edges using seed 20260929.
real_edge_checks.comparison: For each sampled edge and both sides, compare interval-algebra output with brute-force enumeration over the full finite distance band. Exact set equality required.
real_edge_checks.note: This reads coordinates/tracks only; no RNA/ATAC matrix values or correspondence.

uniformity_check.rule: On small fixtures with known A, generate 100000 sub-seed draws and verify each admissible integer start is sampled according to the discrete uniform distribution using a predeclared chi-square goodness-of-fit diagnostic.
uniformity_check.interpretation: A failure blocks execution; the threshold is a software-test diagnostic only and has no biological meaning.

failure_path_tests: computed cardinality disagrees with enumerated cardinality -> STOP
CONTROL_B used to rescue CONTROL_A -> STOP
